stage: Stage 1 - end-to-end pipeline baseline (detect->pair+correct->triangulate->predict) on real Pi 5 hardware
headline_numbers: Detection: 88.66-89.80ms/frame/cam (mean 89.39ms) vs 16.6ms (60fps) budget = ~5.4x OVER. Pair+correct: 1.20-2.60ms. Triangulate: 0.13-4.89ms. Single-shot Model-C fit (bare, no RANSAC): 21.9-101.2ms (comfortably inside 480ms actuation budget). RANSAC-wrapped fit (15 iterations, production RANSAC_N_ITERATIONS["C"]): 335.3-1175.3ms - EXCEEDS the 480ms budget for the longer flights (n_pairs>=44).
notes: First real end-to-end pipeline replay on the Pi, 8 flights spanning n_pairs=15-89 (both gym sessions, spread by frame count). Reuses real production code unmodified (detector_core.py, pixel_velocity_correction.build_corrected_pairs, label_vs_detection.triangulate, trajectory_fit.build_model_fit_predict+ransac_fit) via a repo-structure-mirroring transfer to the Pi - see decision log 55-58. Detection cost is ~97% inside compute_mask() (threshold+morph-open+morph-close+exclusion, bundled) - root cause found in the mask-breakdown row below. RANSAC cost scales with flight length (more pairs = longer ODE integration per scoring pass, see decision 62's theory discussion) - not yet addressed, RANSAC n_iterations sweep still pending (Task 2). Total wall clock across all 8 flights: 111.6s, dominated by RANSAC's 15 iterations/flight.

stage: Stage 2 - Pi vs laptop correctness diff (not a timing measurement - included for completeness per request to backfill all stages)
headline_numbers: 0 detection mismatches, 0.0000px max 2D centroid delta, 0.0000mm max 3D triangulated-point delta - across ALL 8 flights, both cams, every frame. Laptop OpenCV 4.13.0 vs Pi OpenCV 4.10.0.
notes: Confirms the OpenCV version mismatch (4.13.0 laptop / 4.10.0 Pi) flagged during planning is BENIGN for this detect+triangulate pipeline - bit-identical output, nothing to fix. Efficiency note: did not re-run anything on the Pi - reused the Pi's already-saved raw per-frame detections from Stage 1's results JSON, ran the same detector locally on the laptop, diffed. For the 3D comparison, triangulated BOTH streams (Pi's and laptop's 2D detections) locally through the same deterministic triangulate() call, isolating whether DETECTION differs without needing the Pi's own triangulated output at all.

stage: compute_mask breakdown - elliptical vs rectangular close-kernel A/B test
headline_numbers: Per-frame cam0 mask cost (threshold+morph-open+morph-close+exclusion), median across n=448 pairs pooled over all 8 flights. PRODUCTION path (MORPH_ELLIPSE close, 30x30): 86.66ms total (threshold 0.499 + morph-open 1.205 + morph-close 84.051 + exclusion 0.905). ALTERNATIVE (MORPH_RECT close, same 30x30 size, branch test run alongside production, NOT fed into detection): 7.38ms total (morph-close alone drops from 84.051ms to 4.768ms) - a 17.6x reduction on that one substep, from shape alone.
notes: Confirms (empirically, not just theorized) that morph-close's elliptical kernel is ~97% of the mask bottleneck (84.05ms of 86.66ms) and that the bottleneck is kernel SHAPE, not size - a same-size shape-only swap (MORPH_ELLIPSE->MORPH_RECT, both 30x30) very nearly fixes the entire detection-budget overrun on its own (86.66ms -> 7.38ms, would bring total detection comfortably inside the 16.6ms budget). Separability hypothesis CONFIRMED, decision log 63. Timing-only instrumented mirror of compute_mask()'s exact cv2 call sequence - detector_core.py itself untouched. NOT YET VALIDATED: whether a rectangular structuring element preserves detection accuracy close to the validated 0.9208 recall / 0.9751 combined rate - a real open question before recommending this swap for production, flagged but not checked yet.
